stemMd: A cinema will lower weekday ticket prices. Since weekend screenings regularly sell out, management expects empty weekday seats to be filled by new customers without reducing weekend revenue. Which fact most weakens that expectation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Many current weekend patrons say they would switch to weekdays at the lower price.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Some weekday screenings currently have empty seats.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The cinema sells refreshments on every day.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The building has a fixed number of seats.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The same films are often shown on weekdays and weekends.

explanationMd: The expectation treats weekday gains as entirely additional. Switching by current weekend patrons could reduce full-price weekend sales, undermining the no-loss assumption.

distractorRationale.b: This is consistent with the opportunity described.
distractorRationale.c: Refreshment availability does not show whether patronage shifts.
distractorRationale.e: Similarity alone is less direct than evidence of actual switching.
distractorRationale.d: Capacity does not determine how existing customers respond.
